text:
morgan: Heads-up — running the python sampleapp I noticed request IDs vanish in later logs when the OpenTelemetry hook/redaction runs. Repro below, curious if anyone has seen this.

jasper: @morgan :eyes: can you paste the exact logs + env?

morgan: sure — minimal repro (I send X-Request-Id header, first log line has it, subsequent lines become blank):
```
2026-08-12T10:12:01Z INFO sampleapp.request request_id=abc123 start handling /predict
2026-08-12T10:12:01Z INFO sampleapp.runtime request_id= abc123 tokens=12
2026-08-12T10:12:01Z INFO sampleapp.handler request_id= - handled ok
```

morgan: env: PYTHON_SDK=redwood-python-sdk==0.9.2, OTEL_PROPAGATORS=tracecontext,baggage, REDWOOD_REDACTION_HEADERS="authorization,x-forwarded-for,request-id"

sam: Which field do we actually propagate into logger context? header name vs context key mismatch is a common gotcha.

morgan: logger uses context key "req_id" (from middleware) — middleware reads X-Request-Id header and sets req_id. I think the redaction step runs after propagation and deletes the header/key. Node sampleapp (node-sdk 0.8.6) doesn't hit this.

leo: This smells like our redaction utility mutating the request context instead of making a sanitized copy. We changed REDACT_HEADERS parsing in last patch to accept canonical names and sometimes strip "x-". If REDWOOD_REDACTION_HEADERS contains "request-id" it may match and drop the header entirely.

morgan: I tested toggling REDWOOD_REDACTION_HEADERS — removing "request-id" keeps req_id in logs. So definitely related. But we shouldn't make customers have to remove it.

jasper: quick workaround for now: set REDWOOD_LOG_REDACT=false or update REDWOOD_REDACTION_HEADERS to only include the exact headers you want stripped (with x- prefix). I'll open an issue.

jasper: Filed INF-3219. Short description: "python-sdk: redaction hook mutates request context and removes propagated request id". I'll push a minimal fix that copies headers before redaction.

devx-bot: INF-3219 created by jasper — https://redwood.company/infra/INF-3219

jasper: Proposed patch (diff):
```py
# old
for h in headers_to_redact:
    if h in request.headers:
        del request.headers[h]
# new - don't mutate request.headers
for h in headers_to_redact:
    if h in request.headers:
        request.sanitized_headers[h] = "[redacted]"
```

sam: Nice, that should preserve propagation. Can you also make the redaction config accept both canonical and x- prefixes robustly? Some customers send X-Request-Id, others Request-Id.

jasper: yes — will normalize by lowercasing + ensuring both variants are considered. Also adding test that X-Request-Id survives logging context.

leo: Quick note — OTEL_PROPAGATORS differences mean some customers use traceparent vs b3; ensure our middleware only touches headers we intend to redact and never the propagation headers used by otel unless explicitly configured.

morgan: thanks all, repro + workaround documented in the ticket. planning to validate fix locally and then cut a patch release for python sdk.

sam: ack. let's aim for a patch release this week. I'll add to release board. :thumbsup:

devx-bot: Release task created: RDW-RELEASE-873 (contains INF-3219)

morgan: added a small integration test I used in the ticket, will push after review.

jasper: pushed PR, CI green, tagging reviewers @sam @leo.

sam: reviewing today. if green we'll roll to private and hosted customers with next micro patch.

leo: nice catch. once patched we should add a short bit to the onboarding sampleapp README about REDACTION config and common header names (x-request-id vs request-id).
